To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) realism of video games has an impact on attention, retention, and aggressive outcomes; (2) realism of video game is related to the degree of presence experienced while playing; and (3) realism of video gaming has an impact on aggressive outcomes, mediated by attention, retention and presence.
Playing a violent video game (Doom 3) results in more aggression than not playing any game, playing a less realistic violent video game (DOOM) or playing a nonviolent game.

1) those who played Doom III perceived it as more realistic than those playing Doom II, 2) those who played either version of Doom were more attentive and experienced greater presence than those who did not play a game, 3) those who played the more realistic Doom III were more aggressive than those who played the less realistic Doom II, and 4) the effects of game realism and attention on aggression depended on the type of aggression.
